title: The British theologians: God's special mercy toward the elect
source_text: XLIX. Addunt ne electos quidem ipsos in hisce praecedaneis ad regenerationem actibus ita se gerere unquam, quin propter negligentiam & resistentiam suam possint juste a Deo deseri & derelinqui: sed eam esse erga illos specialem Dei misericordiam, ut quamvis hanc gratiam excitantem & illuminantem repellant aliquamdiu, aut suffocent, eos tamen iterum, iterumque urgeat Deus, nec desistat promovere, donec eosdem gratiae suae prorsus subjugaverit, ac in statu filiorum regeneratorum collocaverit.
pass_a_gloss: XLIX. They add that not even the elect themselves ever so conduct themselves in these preceding acts toward regeneration, but that on account of their negligence & resistance they could justly be deserted & forsaken by God: but that such is the special mercy of God toward them, that although they repel this exciting & illuminating grace for some while, or suffocate it, God yet urges them again, and again, nor ceases to advance them, until he has wholly subjugated them to his grace, and placed them in the state of regenerate sons.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLIX. They add that even the elect never behave in these acts that go before regeneration so well that God could not justly abandon and forsake them for their negligence and resistance.

But God's special mercy toward them is such that, though they push away or smother this stirring and enlightening grace for a time, he presses them again and again and does not stop leading them forward until he has brought them wholly under his grace and set them in the state of regenerate children.
